title: Tahini cookies
subtitle: sesame-rich shortbread-style biscuits with a crumbly, melting texture
excerpt: Tahini cookies have a distinctive sesame flavour and a crumbly, almost shortbread-like texture. Tahini replaces most of the butter, which makes the dough softer and more spreadable than standard biscuit dough. The cookies are rolled in sesame seeds before baking, which adds crunch and emphasises the sesame flavour.
sourceNotes: Tahini cookies, informed by Middle Eastern and Greek sesame biscuit traditions. Method adapted for British home baking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thick paste made from ground sesame seeds. It has a nutty, slightly bitter flavour and a high fat content that makes it useful in baking as a partial substitute for butter.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked cookies in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 1 week. Flavour improves after a day as the sesame mellows.

content.text: . Stir the tahini jar thoroughly before measuring, as the oil and solids separate on standing. If your tahini is very thick or dry (some brands are drier than others), the dough will be slightly stiffer; add 1 tablespoon of water to bring it together. The dough is soft and needs a 30-minute rest in the fridge to firm enough to roll into balls.
Beat together the tahini, caster sugar, and icing sugar until well combined. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract.
Add the flour and baking powder and mix until a soft dough forms. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes until firm enough to roll.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line two baking trays with baking parchment.

Spread the sesame seeds on a plate. Roll the dough into balls about 3 cm in diameter. Roll each ball in the sesame seeds and place on the prepared trays, leaving 4 cm between each as they spread slightly. Flatten each ball lightly with the base of a glass.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until golden at the edges and set on top. They will be very soft when warm; leave to cool on the trays for 10 minutes before moving.

attrs.problem: Cookies spreading very flat and thin in the oven
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the refrigerating step; chilled dough holds its shape better.
attrs.fix: Return the dough to the fridge for a further 20 minutes before shaping the remaining cookies.

attrs.problem: Dough too dry to come together
attrs.avoid: Avoid using tahini that has dried out; good tahini should be runny and smooth.
attrs.fix: Add 1 tablespoon of water at a time and mix until the dough just comes together.
